[FARRA:v3p205/r4] FARRA, d. 207 · علي | prefers | A report attributed to Ali identifies them as children; al-Farra finds this more plausible because children had no deeds to bind them, and their question about sinners supports it. | mentions 74:40, 74:41, 74:42

[NAHHAS:v5p72/r10] NAHHAS, d. 338 · ابن الزبير | reports | Ibn ʿUyayna reports ʿAmr ibn Dīnār hearing Ibn al-Zubayr's interpretive reading; the transmission is sound.
[NAHHAS:v5p72/r9] NAHHAS, d. 338 · author | holds | The question 'what brought you to Saqar?' is spoken by people who did not sin.

[RAZI-FULL:v30p185#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | One parse treats “about” as an extra particle: they ask the criminals directly, “What brought you into Saqar?”
[RAZI-FULL:v30p185#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · صاحب الكشاف | reports | Alternatively, the people of the right ask one another about the criminals; al-Kashshaf answers that the criminals recount what happened between them and the questioners.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p185#2/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | A further possibility is that the people of the right asked where the criminals were, then addressed them when they saw them.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p185#2/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The many implicit elements in the exchange exemplify how often the Qur'an leaves material understood from context.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The question adds rebuke and humiliation; it asks what detained them in this depth of the Fire.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The failures to pray and feed the poor mean neglect of obligatory prayer and zakat, since people cannot be punished for omitting non-obligatory acts.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Their joining those who “delved” means engaging in falsehoods.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The “certainty” that finally came to them means death; they denied the resurrection until dying. | mentions 15:99
[RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The wording apparently says that each member of those groups possessed all four listed traits.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · أصحابنا | holds | The author's school cites this verse to argue that unbelievers are punished for neglecting the subsidiary rules of religious law; he says the detailed treatment is in al-Mahsul.
[RAZI-FULL:v30p186/r7] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Although denial of judgment is the worst fault, it comes last to stress that they persisted in it after the preceding three traits. | mentions 90:17

[QURTUBI-FULL:74:39-44/r15] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | reports | Alternatively, believers ask angels about their relatives, and the angels in turn ask the polytheists what put them in Saqar.

[NASAFI-FULL:v4p298/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The question is not itself a report of the believers asking about sinners; it quotes what those questioned report saying to the sinners and what they answered. The narration is elliptical, as Qurʾānic style often is.
[NASAFI-FULL:v4p298/r3] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · قيل | reports | Another analysis treats ʿan as an extra particle.

[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p273/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The criminals say they did not pray or feed the poor, meaning they neither worshipped God nor did good to fellow humans.
[BURHAN:v1p255/r7] BURHAN, d. 794 · author | holds | A single word contains two kāfs without an intervening letter only in the cited forms مناسككم and ما سلككم.

[BIQAI-FULL:v8p236/r3] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The question lets the saved learn the damned person's own account, increasing their gratitude and serving as a warning to listeners.
[DURR-FULL:v8p337/r10] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | In Anas's report, the lowest-ranking person in Hell would ransom himself with the earth's weight in gold, but God recalls easier requests for help and forgiveness that he never made or feared; no one is worse than him. | mentions 74:42, 74:43, 74:44, 74:45, 74:46, 74:47, 74:48

[BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · يروى | reports | A report says God shows Paradise's inhabitants the people of Hell while they are in Hell, and they ask what led them into Saqar.
[BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r2] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The question is asked to reproach and intensify the sinners' regret, and to make the account a warning for its hearers.
[BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | سلككم means inserted you into it, from inserting a thread into a needle; it derives from اسلك, not from سلوك meaning to walk.

[BURSEVI:v10p185#2/r5] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | Abū ʿAmr assimilates the first ك into the next in سلككم; the other readers pronounce both distinctly.
[ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The question can directly explain what the blessed ask, without inserting “saying”; alternatively an implied “saying” clause is circumstantial after “they ask one another.”
[ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | One view makes the questioners a group of angels, with the words reporting what the blessed say the angels asked the criminals; the answer is elaborated to make the account more convincing.
[ALUSI-FULL:v29p132#3/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | rejects | The question may be genuinely reciprocal, with one group asking another about the criminals; treating the words as quoted speech is needlessly strained, though omission is common in revelation.

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r3] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The reciprocal form can mean the people of the right ask one another about the sinners, with “what put you in Saqar?” explaining their question.

[IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p325/r9] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | On the collective reading, the object is omitted and recoverable from the mention of the criminals: they ask about why the criminals entered Saqar.
